anomalies.observed: On display.kicad_sch the SSD1306 interface-select pins are strapped to the wrong rails: BS0 (pin 10) is wired to the VCC rail, BS1 (pin 11) is wired to the GND symbol, and BS2 (pin 12) is wired to the VCC rail, i.e. BS[2:0] = 1,0,1.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the display is configured for I2C by hard-wiring BS0 (pin 10) -> GND, BS1 (pin 11) -> VCC, BS2 (pin 12) -> GND (BS[2:0]=0,1,0), and the MCU drives it over a 2-wire bus (PB13=DISP_SCL on D0, PB14=DISP_SDA on D1/D2). The strap pins must be tied to the opposite rails.

evidence.quote: BS0 (pin 10) -> GND; BS1 (pin 11) -> VCC; BS2 (pin 12) -> GND ... That BS2,BS1,BS0 = 0,1,0 strapping ... is the SSD1306's documented I2C-mode pin configuration
display.kicad_sch (page 5): BS0 pin 10 wire joins the VCC rail at top-right; BS1 pin 11 wire joins the GND symbol; BS2 pin 12 wire joins the VCC rail

anomalies.impact: The OLED driver is left in a non-I2C (SPI/parallel) interface mode, so the MCU's two-wire signals on D0/D1/D2 are not interpreted as SCL/SDA and the display will not communicate or show information.

parsed.summary: The one behaviour-changing deviation I can read off the drawing is the SSD1306 interface-select strapping on display.kicad_sch: BS0/BS1/BS2 are tied to VCC/GND/VCC instead of the GND/VCC/GND (0,1,0) I2C strap the spec requires, which would put the OLED in the wrong bus mode.
